title: A Unified Model for Personalization: Language-Steerable Generative Recommendation, Search, and User Understanding

problem.claim: Deploying one end-to-end model that jointly supports recommendation, retrieval, and reasoning over large, heterogeneous catalogs is challenging.

gap.claim: Text-only generation struggles with item grounding, multiple entity types, latency, and reliability, while tool-augmented systems add orchestration complexity and limit end-to-end optimization.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are increasingly applied to recommendation, retrieval, and reasoning.
A unified system must reference real items unambiguously, handle multiple entity types, and meet strict latency and reliability requirements.
Tool-augmented recommender systems address parts of the problem but add orchestration complexity and constrain end-to-end optimization.

unknowns: The proposed model or system design is not described.
No empirical results, datasets, baselines, or evaluation metrics are provided.
The abstract does not establish whether latency and reliability requirements are met.
User understanding and language steerability are not explained beyond the title.
